question: What is the freemium-to-paid conversion formula, and when does freemium destroy margins?
answer:
## Freemium Conversion Math Freemium *looks* like customer acquisition shortcut but is a **margin trap** if conversion target < **8%**. SaaStr database of 300+ freemium products: teams targeting 2–5% conversion burn **3x** the infrastructure cost per paid customer vs. those hitting **12%+** conversion. Freemium breaks into two buckets: **Product-Led Growth (PLG)** - Goal: **10–15%** conversion via product friction - Freemium tier: 60–90 days full feature access or usage cap at "aha moment" trigger - Example: Notion (unlimited free if <1M notes), Slack (message history limit) - CAC: $8–15 (low), onboarding cost high (self-serve) **Sales-Assisted Freemium** - Goal: **3–8%** conversion (relies on outbound trigger) - Freemium tier: limited users, read-only mode, or reporting gaps - Example: HubSpot (free CRM, conversion via sales outreach) - CAC: $30–60 (sales-touched), onboarding cost moderate Force Management research: **98%** of freemium failures share one trait—the free tier doesn't reach the aha moment. Aha moment = first insight that changes buying intent. If your free tier ends *before* the aha, conversion dies. Conversion formula: ``` Target Conversion Rate = (CAC Payback Period in Months × LTV Multiplier) / 100 If CAC = $50, LTV = $1,500: Payback = $50 / ($1,500 / 24 months) = 0.8 months (24 days) Target Conversion = (0.8 × 3) / 100 = 2.4%? NO—too low. Revise: If 2% converts: $1M freemium spend → 20K accounts → 400 paid CAC actual = $1M / 400 = $2,500/customer Payback = 20 months (unsustainable) ``` The break-even math: | Metric | Healthy | At-Risk | Failing | |--------|---------|---------|----------| | Freemium → Paid Conversion | 10%+ | 5–8% | <3% | | Days to Aha in Free Tier | <14 | 14–21 | >30 | | CAC Payback (months) | <12 | 12–18 | >24 | | MRR per Free → Paid | $150+ | $80–150 | <$80 | | Free Tier Churn/Month | 8–12% | 15–20% | >25% | **When freemium destroys margins:** 1. **Aha moment outside free tier** — Customer hits feature cap or time limit before they understand value. They churn, never convert. 2. **Tier confusion** — Free tier has so many limits ("only 2 projects, 1 user, 1 report") that even power users feel trapped, not tempted. Result: they try a competitor's paid offering instead. 3. **Infrastructure burn** — Each free account costs **$8–12/month** in compute + storage + support (free tier gets forum/email support). At 2% conversion, breakeven requires **$400–600 LTV**. Most B2B SaaS targets $3K+ LTV, so you need 10%+ conversion to profit. 4. **Free tier becomes competitor moat** — If your free tier is too good, Enterprise buyers use it for *one team* without upgrading (Slack message history is free for 90 days; some teams never upgrade, they just archive and reset). ```mermaid flowchart TD A[New Free Signup] B{Does free tier

go paid-only] A --> B B --> C B --> D C --> E D --> E E -->|Yes| F E -->|No| G F --> H D --> I C --> J J --> K K -->|Yes| L K -->|No| M G --> M ``` **Challenger playbook**: If your free tier conversion is 3–5%, **kill it.** Offer a **14-day paid trial** instead. Paradox: paid trials convert at **18–22%** because buyers perceive higher stakes. Pavilion data confirms: removing the free tier and launching a paid trial netted **$280K new ARR** in a B2B SaaS firm with $2M prior ARR (12% growth). Why? Sales team focused on trial → paid, not free → trial → paid. **CRO action**: Audit your free tier. Identify the aha moment (first time user discovers ROI). If it happens after day 14, compress the freemium experience. If aha is day 3, expand the free trial to day 21. Measure: conversion rate lift, CAC payback, and net unit economics. If payback >18 months even at 10% conversion, freemium is a loss center. TAGS: freemium,conversion-math,product-led-growth,CAC-payback,LTV-modeling,tier-design,Force-Management,SaaStr
